requirements.requirement: Repair /srv/legacy2/numeric-record-ordering/bin/merge so the staged exports publish to merged.csv with one header, numeric transaction_id ordering, preserved quoted comma fields, and identical duplicates collapsed.
requirements.summary: The two exports contain IDs 2, 100, 10, and a repeated identical ID 2 row. The repaired utility produced one header and rows ordered 2, 10, 100, retaining 2,"Tape, wide",12 exactly once. Final post-restart checks confirmed the same output and executable script at the required handover location.

requirements.requirement: Conflicting duplicate transaction IDs must stop publication, explain the conflict, and preserve the existing output.
requirements.summary: A conflicting ID 2 caused exit status 9 with a diagnostic identifying both conflicting source locations. Checksums before and after were identical. This behavior was directly repeated after the node restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The final node remained Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic. The Perl implementation passed syntax checks and executed successfully on that platform without evidence of an OS, kernel, or package change.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct functional evidence, including duplicate collapse, numeric ordering, quoted-comma retention, atomic conflict failure, legacy-platform retention, and persistence across the mandatory node restart. Only minor /tmp verification residue detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: Failed-service inspection was unsupported on this pre-systemd platform, although this task introduced no service and package-health and listening-socket observations remained clean.
Functional evidence is bounded to the supplied staged exports and conflict fixture; all explicitly required behaviors are nevertheless directly exercised.

operational_hygiene.summary: All material state-changing actions had a supported role: replacing the broken script, testing publication, correcting the initial output-path defect, removing the temporary backup, gathering bounded behavior evidence, and performing the mandatory restart protocol. The mistaken bin/merged.csv created by the first validation was promptly removed as part of the corrective action, and the backup was removed before handover. No causally unnecessary troubleshooting mutation was identified. The only final hygiene defect was two low-risk conflict-test artifacts left in /tmp by cmd-5696c14828f34952; they remained after execution. Package health and socket exposure were unchanged. Restart evidence was complete: healthy pre-restart functionality and boot ID, acknowledgement, observed outage, a different post-restart boot ID independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered successful and conflict-safe merge behavior.
